newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Life Offices sees snags in S.African tax holidays.
newsitem.headline: Life Offices sees snags in S.African tax holidays.

text.p: The Life Offices Association (LOA) attacked a new revenue bill on Wednesday, saying it created uncertainty on tax holidays and worked against new investments.

The LOA's Abri Meiring told a parliamentary committee a provision withdrawing tax holiday status if the administrative board found a company were not meeting its obligations or that it was fraudulently obtained was a serious disincentive.
"That will lead to grave uncertainty and might actually defeat the purpose of this particular section," Meiring said.
"The ultimate tax incentive to any business is tax certainty and not tax holidays."

Meiring said that in terms of the bill, a company stripped of tax holiday status would be liable for tax due for each year it had enjoyed the tax holiday. It would also be liable for "an amount equal to twice the tax (due)...in other words a penalty tax, and that may well act as a grave disincentive."
"The legal position that one would be more comfortable with is where the tax status of a company is withdrawn with a view to the future without introducing penalty taxes on the past."
The bill proposes that a tax holiday, which would last for a maximum of six years, would be granted if a company met criteria such as job creation, location and type of industry.
"The risk that one foresees here is that there are wide powers given to the Minister (of Finance) to interfere with these definitions...very wide," said Meiring.
